1 # PRD: Workflow viewer UX ("Run Story") 2 3 Status: Proposed 2026-09-24. Synthesizes the four-lens audit of the Projects viewer (orientation, chronology, detail-density, live-status; screenshots `shots/01`–`14`, payloads `api/*.json`), three redesign proposals (timeline-first, triage-first, graph-inspector) and two judges' verdicts. Both judges picked **timeline-first** as the base. This PRD adds every graft that fits and respects every `must_avoid`. Where the two judges disagree, Appendix B records the decision. Follows [PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md](PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md), [PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md](PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md), [PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md](PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md) and [PRD_WORKER_LANES.md](PRD_WORKER_LANES.md) (all in `docs/`; this file is meant to land as `docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md`). Their truthfulness rules still hold. This PRD changes only how compactly they are said. 4 5 Revision 2 (2026-09-24) closes the critic's gaps. The changes, each checked against the code: 6 - Node-level interruptions (review, freeze) and repair continuations now get a next step (6.2 rule 5). 7 - A new situation covers runs the controller blocked before freeze (6.2 rule 6, reason source 0, B1). 8 - Pane attention is carried everywhere a question is (6.4, B2 `attention.kind: 'pane'`). 9 - Controller liveness is read-only and PID-reuse safe (B2 `activity.controller`). 10 - The first-screen budget is measured against a one-row Projects header, with the tabs above the graph (4.2). 11 - Slices are file-disjoint when run in parallel, and no slice's test depends on a later slice (11, 12). 12 - B3 moves to a top-level `viewer` key, which survives re-registration. 13 - Test migrations are corrected (12.3). The `answer`, `init` and `status` command wording is fixed, gate reasons without a check id are handled, and two API field claims are corrected. 14 15 Scope: `src/projects/**`, `src/App.tsx` (Projects header only), `src/App.css` and new per-area stylesheets, `tests/project-workflows/**` and `tests/unit/**`. For backend slice S5: `server/projects.ts`, `server/projectsConfig.ts`, `contracts/projects/**` and a new pure module `contracts/projects/triage.ts`. The Python controller (`workflow/*.py`) is **not** changed here. Controller-side gaps are listed as follow-ups C1–C10 (section 9.4). The viewer stays strictly read-only. It never runs a command and never mutates a run. 16 17 ## 1. Problem 18 19 The user's complaint, verbatim: *"Lets work on making the UX better for the workflow section. Its not good, i need to look around to understand whats where when it happened and overall is just bad."* 20 21 The audit confirms each part of the sentence with measurements taken from the live runs. 22 23 **"what's where": nothing answers the operator's question where they land.** 24 - The run page spends its first screen on an 11-fact grid, a 3-sentence legend, a keyboard hint, a duplicate node list and an empty "Select a node…" panel (`04-…-fold.png`, RunView.tsx:98-217). It never names the failing step, the reason or the next command (orientation:run-first-screen-no-answer, live-status:run-why-not-surfaced). 25 - For skeleton-001, the cause ("general blocked: 1 P1, Private matches can be joined without their code") takes a click and about 1.3 screens of scrolling to reach. For workflow-guardrails-001 it sits inside Candidate › Lane ui › error box. 26 - No page tells the operator which CLI command to run next (live-status:no-next-action). 27 28 **"when it happened": the run has no history view.** 29 - Events render only per node, at the bottom of each node page (NodeDetail.tsx:466-487). 30 - Events whose `node_id` is null are dropped everywhere (NodeDetail.tsx:305). In skeleton-001 that is 7 of 26 events, including the controller's diagnosis *"failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 … a code fix is a lane repair (RUNBOOK)"* and *"Repair 1 applied"* (chronology:unattributed-events-hidden, live-status:controller-events-hidden). 31 - No duration is ever computed. Every time is a full UTC ISO string (status.ts:100-104). "Last event" is shown as a sequence number, and "Updated" trails real activity by 3.5 minutes (orientation:no-run-timeline, chronology:no-durations, chronology:last-activity-misleading, chronology:utc-only-absolute-times). 32 33 **"look around": node pages are walls.** 34 - `launch_game` is 19,834 px tall. 77 file panels take 15,400 px of it, and the Markdown files are auto-rendered (detail-density:launch-files-wall). 35 - A worker question sits at y≈19,320 (orientation:pending-question-buried). 36 - On `verify_game` the gate sits behind a repeated worker summary and 10 assumptions (detail-density:worker-narrative-duplicated). 37 - Earlier failed attempts are served by the API (`results/game/1` and `/2` return 200) but cannot be reached from the viewer (orientation:earlier-attempts-unreachable). 38 - The node list wastes a third of the width for the whole page. The graph clips "Integrate candidate" at 1440 px (orientation:navigation-model-node-list, orientation:graph-clipped). 39 - At 390 px the node detail starts at y≈1,975 and the verify page overflows to 427 px wide (orientation:mobile-node-detail-offscreen). 40 41 **"overall just bad": live watching is not trustworthy.** 42 - A worker waiting on a question, or blocked in its pane on a permission prompt or a refusal, looks exactly like a busy one (live-status:question-attention-invisible). 43 - Polling is silent, and a failed poll keeps stale data with no warning. A dead controller cannot be told from a quiet one: during a worker phase, 28 minutes without events is normal (live-status:no-liveness-indicator). 44 - A run the controller stopped before freeze, or interrupted during review or freeze, shows no cause and no command. Its reason is only in a node-less controller row that no page renders (live-status:run-why-not-surfaced, live-status:no-next-action). 45 - Every workflow is titled "Feature implementation" (orientation:naming-feature-implementation). 46 - Reaching a run takes three clicks through near-empty pages (orientation:hierarchy-depth-empty-levels). 47 48 All 23 P1 findings fall into these four themes. Appendix A maps all 72 findings. 49 50 ## 2. Goals and non-goals 51 52 ### Goals 53 54 1. **Answer first.** The first screen of a run page, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, answers five questions: 55 - Where is the run, or where did it stop? 56 - Why? 57 - Since when? 58 - What exactly do I type next, if anything? 59 - Is this page current? 60 2. **One story in time.** At 1440×900 the first screen also shows the Steps table: each step's start, duration and attempt markers. The markers include ⚑ (the controller's diagnosis) and ⚒ (an operator repair) on the step they concern. 61 - The full text of the node-less diagnosis and repair rows is in Activity, directly below Steps on the same default tab, never behind a toggle or a tab. 62 - The guarantee covers runs with up to 2 lanes: every live run so far, and every fixture except `RUN_THREE_LANES`. For those runs the focus step's row is inside the fold; section 4.2 has the measured budget. 63 - With 3 or more lanes the graph grows a row and the focus row can fall below the fold. The Now banner still names the focus step there. 64 - At 390×844 the first screen holds the Now banner, and Steps follow directly. 65 3. **One home per piece of evidence.** Each piece of evidence is shown once, where it answers its question: files on the worker, checks, logs and screenshots on verification, findings on review. Everywhere else it appears as a one-line link or a count. 66 4. **Short node pages.** A node page's first screen shows its verdict, timing, attempts and a section index with counts. Long lists are collapsed and fetch their content only on demand. No node page needs more than about 3 screens before the operator expands something. 67 5. **Live-watch trust.** A freshness chip is always visible. 68 - While a run is running or paused, the chip also says whether its controller process is alive (B2 `activity.controller`; Linux `/proc`, and "unknown" elsewhere). 69 - A worker or reviewer that waits on the operator is visible on the run page, the graph, the Steps and strip rows, the run lists and the browser tab title. That covers a waiting question and a pane that needs attention. 70 6. **Honesty kept, said once.** The rules survive: a worker's success is not workflow completion, a worker's report is as signalled and not verified, the viewer is read-only, executors are marked, inferred times are marked. Each is said once, compactly. 71 7. **Shippable slices.** The existing browser suite stays green in both phases (worker mocks and candidate seeds), apart from assertions this PRD migrates explicitly in the same slice. 72 73 ### Non-goals 74 75 - Starting, answering, approving, retrying, repairing or cancelling anything from the viewer. Commands are shown as text to copy. 76 - Changing the controller, exporter or event vocabulary (`workflow/*.py`). Those gaps are follow-ups C1–C10. Until they land, the viewer infers the missing values and labels every inference. 77 - A liveness claim from PID existence alone, such as `process.kill(pid, 0)` on a PID parsed from event text. PID reuse would give a false "alive". 78 - B2 instead reads `/proc//cmdline` and the process start time. It says "running" only for this run's own `automatic-step` child, started before it logged its PID. It says "unknown" whenever it cannot tell. 79 - A controller heartbeat (C7) would make this portable. 80 - The Pi/Claude skills areas. 81 - Renaming `definition.name`. It feeds `definition_revision` (server/projectsConfig.ts:89-90), so changing it would flag every old run as "definition changed". 82 83 ### Confirmed decisions 84 85 - **The SVG graph stays.** It is fitted to the width by retuning `dag.ts`, not rebuilt as HTML. `.workflow-node-meta`, the aria-label format, `.workflow-node-shape` `stroke-dasharray`, `.is-agent`/`.is-controller` and arrow-key roving are unchanged (clarity.spec.ts:63-109, projects.spec.ts:164-168). 86 - **A one-row Projects header.** On Projects routes the app header is one 48 px row: title, the Pi/Claude/Projects roots and Refresh. The Pi/Claude subtitle is dropped there. The breadcrumb is the only other chrome (28 px). Today the chrome takes about 150 px, or about 180 px with the info line (`04-…-fold.png`). The skills routes keep their header. 87 - **Tabs above the graph.** `[Run] [Assignment]` sit directly under the Now banner. The graph lives inside the Run tabpanel, so it disappears on Assignment and comes back on Run (inputs.spec.ts:56, :89). 88 - **One pipeline view per screen.** On the run page, the graph shows *shape and status* and the Steps table shows *time*. The Steps table is the `run-node-list`, not "the same graph as text". On node pages a sticky step strip replaces the graph, so the graph and the strip never share a screen. There are no lane cards that repeat step durations. 89 - **Views that need a link live in the path.** Tabs and attempts are URL path segments (`/assignment`, `/nodes//attempts/`), because App routing is pathname-only (App.tsx:159). 90 - **Section index, not sub-tabs, on node pages.** Evidence stays in the DOM, Ctrl-F works, and most `toBeVisible` assertions survive. 91 - **Commands follow the RUNBOOK**: `"$PY" -m workflow "$RUN" …`. 92 - `$RUN` stays a placeholder unless a workflow opts into serving its run directory (B3, home-relative, off by default). 93 - A command appears only when a situation rule in section 6 matches the run's *current* state. Otherwise the viewer says "No known next step matched" and links the RUNBOOK section. 94 - **The vocabulary is "attempt"**, the word the controller, CLI and RUNBOOK use. The following wordings are retired: "Graph attempt", "Result attempt 3 (graph node attempt is 1)" and "attempt 0". 95 - **Default times are local**, with the UTC value in the tooltip. A remembered Local/UTC toggle is available. 96 97 ## 3. Information architecture 98 99 ### 3.1 Routes 100 101 `routes.ts` gains three literals. `parseProjectsPathname`, which today rejects any trailing segment (routes.ts:82), accepts `assignment` after a run id (added in S3) and `attempts/` after a node id (added in S4-core). Every URL that works today keeps working. 102 103 | Route | Page | First question it answers | 104 |---|---|---| 105 | `/projects` | **Runs home** | Does anything need me, what is running, what finished recently (all projects)? The only page that carries the read-only note (`projects-info`). | 106 | `/projects/

` | Project | The same run rows for one project, grouped by feature. The group header links to the feature's runs (`workflows-list`). | 107 | `/projects/

/workflows/` | Feature runs | Run rows (`run-list`) with where each run stands, its duration and its age. "Current definition" moves into a closed `

559	### 5.1 Model
560	
561	`contracts/projects/triage.ts` (pure, no React, shared with the server for B2) exports:
562	
563	```ts
564	buildTimeline({ definition, snapshot, events, inputs, review?, laneResults?, now }): {
565	  runStart: Instant; runEnd: Instant | null;             // runEnd = last non-controller activity, never updated_at
566	  spans: Span[];      // one per node attempt: node_id, lane, attempt, start, end, status, outcome, live
567	  markers: Marker[];  // diagnosis | repair | controller_start | controller_error | interrupted | question | answer | log
568	  gaps: Gap[];        // operator | controller_down | waiting_worker | idle, with from/to/ms
569	  byNode: Map<string, Span[]>;
570	}
571	type Instant = { at: string; source: 'event' | 'receipt' | 'check' | 'review' | 'inferred'; note?: string }
572	```
573	
574	It is memoized on `(snapshot.last_sequence, inputs identity, review identity)`, so a 5 s poll that brings nothing new does not rebuild it.

576	### 5.2 Derivation rules
577	
578	Each rule carries its source tag, which the UI shows in a tooltip. Each rule has a unit test on the captured payloads.
579	
580	1. **Attempt number.** Re-read it from the message with `/\battempt (\d+)/i` before falling back to `event.attempt`. The server parser is case-sensitive (server/projects.ts:1067-1070), so every challenge event reads "attempt 1" today. Expected on skeleton-001: challenge attempts 1, 2, 3.
581	2. **Controller rows.** On any node, a message matching `^Automatic checkpoint controller PID \d+` is a `controller_start` marker, never a node status. A `^\[Errno \d+\]` failure on a node that later succeeded is a `controller_error` marker. This fixes guardrails `launch_controller` #5-#17/#24/#29/#32 until B1 lands.
582	3. **Spans.** A `running` status event opens a span for (node, attempt). The next terminal status (succeeded, failed, paused, cancelled) closes it. A new attempt that opens while the previous one is still open closes it as "ended without a record". Example: challenge attempt 1, 08:39:42 → 08:45:55.
583	4. **Receipts and evidence.** When events are missing:
584	   - A worker span runs from `native_started_at` (else `launch_requested_at`) to `stop.confirmed_at`, or to *now* while running. The source is "receipt". Example: 08:50:52 → 09:19:13 = 28m21s.
585	   - A review without events ends at `reviewed_at`. Its start is the earliest `reviewers[].launched_at`, else the end of the step it depends on, marked ≈ inferred.
586	   - A candidate without a `running` event starts ≈ at the end of the last verify step. Example: 09:29:15 → 09:30:21.
587	   - An approval without an event is ≈ an instant at the integrate event's time, with the note "no approval event recorded".
588	5. **Run-level rows** (`node_id` null):
589	   - `failed identically` becomes a **diagnosis** marker (⚑), attached to the lane named in `<phase>/<lane>`.
590	   - `^Repair (\d+) applied` becomes a **repair** marker (⚒). It carries the snapshot and files from the node's `paused` "Repair n by the operator" event (#20).
591	   - `Supervisor interrupted` / `Claude Code was unavailable` become an **interrupted** marker.
592	   - A controller row whose raw status was `blocked` becomes a **controller_blocked** marker (✗). With B1 it is served as `status: 'failed'` on a node-less row. Before B1, it is recognised as a node-less row that is not one of the running-type messages: the PID checkpoint, `^Rerunning `, `^Resuming `, `^Repair \d+ applied`. Examples: `Worker game deadline exhausted; no automatic relaunch` (automatic.py:1284), `… failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 …` (advance_or_block, :1011; this one is also the diagnosis), and `… ended on it in a state no resume continues` (:1323).
593	   - Anything else is a plain log row.
594	6. **Gaps.** A stretch of more than 120 s with no event becomes a gap row, classified by what surrounds it:
595	   - after a diagnosis, failure or pause and before a repair or resume: **operator time**. Example: skeleton-001, 5m37s.
596	   - after a `controller_error` and before a `controller_start`: **controller not running**. Example: guardrails, 4m56s and 6m35s. This applies even inside a worker span, where it is drawn as a hatched band on that bar.
597	   - inside a worker span with no other cause: **worker working**. Example: 28m21s.
598	   - otherwise: **no activity**.
599	
600	   Silences over 30 min get an axis break in the Steps bars, so overnight gaps do not squash the chart.
601	7. **Questions.** Each `asked_at` gets a row ("duel asked question 2 · waited 5m"), and so does each `answered_at`. While `answer === null` the row is live. When the export is stale, the question event message is the fallback (section 6.2, rule 1).
602	8. **Setup and check split** (node view only): attempt start → first `checks[].started_at` is setup; first `started_at` → last `finished_at` is checks. Example: 42 s + 33 s.
603	9. **Worker deadline**: `native_started_at + worker_timeout_seconds + Σ(question waits)`. **Reviewer deadline**: `launched_at + review_timeout_seconds`.
604	10. **Run span**: `created_at` → the last non-controller activity (events, `reviewed_at`, `stop.confirmed_at`). For skeleton-001 that is 52m51s ending 09:32:31, not "Updated 09:36:07".
605	11. **Lane on candidate events.** Until B1 prefixes the lane, candidate failures are matched to lane results by comparing an event's time with each lane result's last `checks[].finished_at`. Guardrails #28 → `candidate_ui/1`, #31 → `candidate_ui/2`.

1	/**
2	 * Run triage (PRD_VIEWER_UX sections 5 and 6): the pure model behind the run page's Now banner, Steps table and
3	 * Activity list, the node pages' attempt strips and the server's run-list activity. No React and no I/O, so the client
4	 * and the server import the same rules and the list headline and the run page agree by construction.
5	 *
6	 * It reads only served contract payloads: the run detail, its events, the run inputs, the review and worker results by
7	 * URI. Where the controller records nothing (a print review's start, an approval, a candidate lane's start) the value is
8	 * inferred and says so (`source: 'inferred'`). Next steps are RUNBOOK commands with the `"$PY"` and `"$RUN"`
9	 * placeholders; every other value the viewer cannot know (a feature name, a run id, a commit, a reason) stays a `<…>`
10	 * placeholder. Nothing here runs a command or changes a run.
11	 */
12	import { isBlockingFinding, type ReviewResult, type RunDetail, type RunInputs, type RunInputWorker } from './v1.ts'
13	import type { WorkerResult, WorkflowEvent } from '../workflow/v1.ts'
14	
15	export type NodeStatus = RunDetail['snapshot']['status']
16	type NodeKind = RunDetail['definition']['nodes'][number]['kind']
17	
18	/** Everything the triage model reads about one run. Only `detail` and `events` are required; the rest refines the answer. */
19	export type RunData = {
20	  detail: RunDetail
21	  events: readonly WorkflowEvent[]
22	  inputs?: RunInputs | null
23	  review?: ReviewResult | null
24	  /** Immutable worker and candidate results keyed by their result URI (`…/results/<lane>/<k>`, `…/results/candidate_<lane>/<k>`). */
25	  results?: ReadonlyMap<string, WorkerResult>
26	}
27	
28	// ---- Timeline types (5.1) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	
30	/** Where a time comes from; the UI shows the source in a tooltip and prefixes inferred values with `≈`. */
31	export type InstantSource = 'event' | 'receipt' | 'check' | 'review' | 'inferred'
32	export type Instant = { at: string; source: InstantSource; note?: string }
33	/** A node status, or `no_record` for an attempt a later attempt replaced before any verdict was recorded. */
34	export type SpanStatus = NodeStatus | 'no_record'
35	
36	/** One attempt of one node (for the candidate: of one lane). `end` is null while it runs; `ms` is null until both ends are known. */
37	export type Span = {
38	  node_id: string
39	  lane: string | null
40	  attempt: number
41	  start: Instant | null
42	  end: Instant | null
43	  ms: number | null
44	  status: SpanStatus
45	  /** The humanized message that closed the span (or, while it runs, the latest one). */
46	  outcome: string
47	  live: boolean
48	  /** The result this attempt produced, when its URI is known (verify attempts, matched candidate lanes). */
49	  result_uri: string | null
50	  /** 5.2 rule 8, when the attempt's result is loaded: attempt start → first check start, first check start → last check finish. */
51	  split: { setup_ms: number; checks_ms: number } | null
52	}
53	
54	export type MarkerKind = 'diagnosis' | 'repair' | 'controller_start' | 'controller_error' | 'controller_blocked' | 'interrupted' | 'question' | 'answer' | 'log'
55	
56	/** A moment that is not a node status: controller rows (5.2 rules 2 and 5) and worker questions and answers (rule 7). */
57	export type Marker = {
58	  kind: MarkerKind
59	  at: string
60	  /** The event it came from; null for question and answer rows read from the run inputs. */
61	  sequence: number | null
62	  /** The node it concerns: a diagnosis or repair names the lane's verify or candidate node; null for the controller itself. */
63	  node_id: string | null
64	  lane: string | null
65	  /** A controller row: served without a node, or (before B1) aliased onto a lane named `controller`. */
66	  run_level: boolean
67	  /** The controller wrote it as `blocked` (served `failed` with B1): 6.2 reason source 0. */
68	  blocked: boolean
69	  message: string
70	  raw: string
71	  repair?: { n: number; snapshot: string | null; files: string[] }
72	  question?: { n: number; text: string; asked_at: string; answered_at: string | null; wait_ms: number | null; live: boolean; exported: boolean }
73	}
74	
75	/** A silence over two minutes, classified by what surrounds it (5.2 rule 6). `lanes` are the workers it overlaps. */
76	export type GapKind = 'operator' | 'controller_down' | 'waiting_worker' | 'idle'
77	export type Gap = { kind: GapKind; from: string; to: string; ms: number; lanes: string[] }
78	
79	/** One Activity row, oldest first. `controller_log` rows (PID checkpoints) sit behind the "Controller log (n)" toggle. */
80	export type ActivityRow = {
81	  at: string
82	  source: InstantSource
83	  sequence: number | null
84	  node_id: string | null
85	  lane: string | null
86	  attempt: number | null
87	  kind: 'start' | 'end' | 'update' | 'marker' | 'gap'
88	  status: SpanStatus | null
89	  marker: MarkerKind | null
90	  text: string
91	  /** The served message, for the expander; null for rows built from receipts, the review or the inputs. */
92	  raw: string | null
93	  /** The closed span's duration on `end` rows, the silence on `gap` rows. */
94	  ms: number | null
95	  inferred: boolean
96	  controller_log: boolean
97	  gap: Gap | null
98	}
99	
100	export type Timeline = {
101	  runStart: Instant
102	  /** The last non-controller activity of a finished run (never `updated_at`); null while the run can still move. */
103	  runEnd: Instant | null
104	  /** The latest moment that is not a PID checkpoint, with its humanized text in `note`. */
105	  lastActivity: Instant | null
106	  spans: Span[]
107	  markers: Marker[]
108	  gaps: Gap[]
109	  byNode: ReadonlyMap<string, Span[]>

304	// ---- humanizeEvent (5.3) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
305	
306	type Phrase = [RegExp, (...groups: string[]) => string]
307	const PHRASES: Phrase[] = [
308	  [/^Awaiting explicit completion signal; idle is not acceptance$/, () => 'waiting for the worker\'s completion signal (idle is not acceptance)'],
309	  [/^Launching or reconciling the exact native session$/, () => 'launching the native session'],
310	  [PID_ROW, pid => `controller started (PID ${pid})`],
311	  [/^Attempt (\d+); revision (\S+)$/, (k, revision) => `attempt ${k} started · revision ${revision}`],
312	  [/^Required tests and artifacts passed; recorded for the candidate gate: (.+)$/, checks => `passed · ${checks} gated at the candidate`],
313	  [/^Combined revision (\S+)$/, revision => `combined revision ${revision}`],
314	  [/^Fast-forwarded to (\S+); no push performed$/, commit => `fast-forwarded to ${commit} · no push performed`],
315	  [/^Immutable snapshots captured; worker-reported checks are not trusted$/, () => 'snapshots captured (worker-reported checks are not trusted)'],
316	  [/^Native workers stopped before snapshot capture: (.+)$/, lanes => `workers stopped before snapshot capture: ${lanes}`],
317	  [/^Design challenge attempt (\d+): one print job, session (\S+)$/, (k, session) => `attempt ${k} started (print job, session ${session})`],
318	  [/^Feature files re-pinned for design challenge attempt (\d+) on base (\S+)$/, (k, base) => `attempt ${k} started after re-pinning the feature files (base ${base})`],
319	  [/^Design challenge attempt (\d+) passed \((\d+) (P\d) concern\(s\)\); launching workers$/, (k, n, severity) => `attempt ${k} passed · ${n} ${severity} ${Number(n) === 1 ? 'concern' : 'concerns'}`],
320	  [/^Design challenge attempt (\d+) paused the run before any worker launch: (\d+) P0\/P1 concern\(s\)$/,
321	    (k, n) => `attempt ${k} paused the run: ${n} P0/P1 ${Number(n) === 1 ? 'concern' : 'concerns'}; no worker launched`],
322	  [/^KeyboardInterrupt$/, () => 'interrupted (KeyboardInterrupt)'],
323	  [/^[0-9a-f]{8}(?:-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}(?:, [0-9a-f]{8}(?:-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12})*$/, () => 'verdict recorded'],
324	  [/^\[Errno (\d+)\] No such file or directory: (.+)$/, (n, what) => `[Errno ${n}] ${what} not found`],
325	  [/^(?:worker|candidate)\/([a-z][a-z0-9-]*) (failed identically on attempts \d+ and \d+); not transient, inspect \S+ ?(.*)$/, (lane, what, rest) => `${lane} ${what}; not transient. ${rest}`.trim()],
326	  [/^Repair (\d+) by the operator: snapshot (\S+) = (\S+) \+ (\S+) on \S+ \S+ \(([^)]*)\)[\s\S]*$/,
327	    (n, snapshot, base, fix, files) => `repair ${n}: snapshot ${snapshot} = ${base} + ${fix} (${plural(files.split(', ').length, 'file')})`],
328	]
329	/** 40/64-character SHAs and 8-character abbreviations; session UUIDs are matched first and kept whole. */
330	const HASHES = /\b[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\b|\b(?=[0-9a-f]*[a-f])[0-9a-f]{8,64}\b/g
331	
332	/** An event message for people: known controller phrases reworded, the `[<lane>] ` B1 prefix dropped, SHAs cut to 7 characters. */
333	export function humanizeEvent(event: Pick<WorkflowEvent, 'message'>): string {
334	  const message = event.message.replace(/^\[[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\] /, '')
335	  let text = message
336	  for (const [pattern, render] of PHRASES) {
337	    const match = pattern.exec(message)
338	    if (match) { text = render(...match.slice(1)); break }
339	  }
340	  return text.replace(HASHES, hash => hash.includes('-') ? hash : hash.slice(0, 7))
341	}

343	// ---- Event classification (5.2 rules 1, 2 and 5) ------------------------------------------------------------------
344	
345	type Row = {
346	  event: WorkflowEvent
347	  /** The node whose history it belongs to; null for controller rows (see `Marker.run_level`). */
348	  node: string | null
349	  status: NodeStatus | null
350	  /** Rule 1: re-read from the message, else null (the served `event.attempt` is case-sensitive before B1). */
351	  attempt: number | null
352	  marker: MarkerKind | null
353	  blocked: boolean
354	  text: string
355	}
356	
357	function classify(detail: RunDetail, events: readonly WorkflowEvent[]): Row[] {
358	  const sorted = [...events].sort((a, b) => a.sequence - b.sequence)
359	  const lastPid = Math.max(0, ...sorted.filter(event => PID_ROW.test(event.message)).map(event => event.sequence))
360	  const lastSucceeded = new Map<string, number>()
361	  for (const event of sorted) if (event.node_id && event.status === 'succeeded') lastSucceeded.set(event.node_id, event.sequence)
362	  const nodeStatus = new Map(detail.snapshot.nodes.map(node => [node.node_id, node.status]))
363	  return sorted.map(event => {
364	    const message = event.message
365	    // An [Errno] failure the controller came back from (a later checkpoint, or the node succeeded after all) is its own error, not a verdict.
366	    const recovered = lastPid > event.sequence || (event.node_id !== null
367	      && (nodeStatus.get(event.node_id) === 'succeeded' || (lastSucceeded.get(event.node_id) ?? 0) > event.sequence))
368	    const row = (marker: MarkerKind | null, node: string | null, status: NodeStatus | null, blocked = false): Row => ({
369	      event, node, status, marker, blocked, attempt: marker ? null : Number(ATTEMPT.exec(message)?.[1] ?? NaN) || null, text: humanizeEvent(event),
370	    })
371	    const runLevel = event.node_id === null || (event.node_id === CONTROLLER_LANE_NODE && CONTROLLER_LANE_ROWS.some(pattern => pattern.test(message)))
372	    if (PID_ROW.test(message)) return row('controller_start', null, null)
373	    if (runLevel) {
374	      // Before B1 a node-less row has no status; with B1 the controller's own status is kept (blocked → failed, interrupted → paused).
375	      const status = event.status
376	      if (IDENTICAL.test(message)) return row('diagnosis', null, status, true)
377	      if (REPAIR_APPLIED.test(message)) return row('repair', null, status)
378	      if (INTERRUPTED_ROW.test(message) || status === 'paused') return row('interrupted', null, status)
379	      if (ERRNO_ROW.test(message) && recovered) return row('controller_error', null, status)
380	      if (status === 'failed' || (status === null && !RUNNING_ROWS.some(pattern => pattern.test(message)))) return row('controller_blocked', null, status, true)
381	      return row('log', null, status)
382	    }
383	    if (event.status === 'failed' && recovered && (ERRNO_ROW.test(message) || STOP_UNCONFIRMED.test(message))) return row('controller_error', event.node_id, null)
384	    return row(null, event.node_id, event.status)
385	  })
386	}

388	// ---- buildTimeline (5.1, 5.2) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

390	type Internal = { rows: Row[]; lastActivityText: string | null }
391	const INTERNAL = new WeakMap<Timeline, Internal>()
392	const TIMELINES = new Map<string, { key: readonly unknown[]; timeline: Timeline }>()
393	const TIMELINE_CACHE_SIZE = 32
394	
395	/**
396	 * The run's history as spans (one per node attempt), markers, gaps and Activity rows. Memoized per run on the served
397	 * state (last sequence, node states, the event count, and the inputs, review and results objects by identity), so a
398	 * poll that brings nothing new returns the same object. Treat the result as read-only.
399	 */
400	export function buildTimeline(run: RunData): Timeline {
401	  const { summary, snapshot, definition } = run.detail
402	  const id = `${summary.project_id}/${summary.workflow_id}/${summary.run_id}`
403	  const key = [snapshot.last_sequence, snapshot.status, snapshot.nodes.map(node => `${node.status}:${node.attempt}:${node.result_uri ?? ''}`).join(','),
404	    definition.definition_revision, summary.created_at, run.events.length, run.events.at(-1)?.sequence, run.inputs ?? null, run.review ?? null, run.results ?? null]
405	  const cached = TIMELINES.get(id)
406	  if (cached && cached.key.every((value, index) => value === key[index])) return cached.timeline
407	  const timeline = computeTimeline(run)
408	  TIMELINES.delete(id)
409	  TIMELINES.set(id, { key, timeline })
410	  if (TIMELINES.size > TIMELINE_CACHE_SIZE) TIMELINES.delete(TIMELINES.keys().next().value!)
411	  return timeline
412	}
413	
414	function newSpan(nodeId: string, lane: string | null, attempt: number, start: Instant | null): Span {
415	  return { node_id: nodeId, lane, attempt, start, end: null, ms: null, status: 'running', outcome: '', live: false, result_uri: null, split: null }
416	}
417	
418	function close(span: Span, status: SpanStatus, end: Instant, outcome: string) {
419	  span.status = status
420	  span.end = end
421	  span.outcome = outcome
422	  span.ms = span.start ? Math.max(0, ms(end.at) - ms(span.start.at)) : null
423	}
424	
425	function reviewOutcome(review: ReviewResult): string {
426	  const counts = (['P0', 'P1', 'P2'] as const).map(severity => [severity, review.findings.filter(finding => finding.severity === severity).length] as const)
427	    .filter(([, count]) => count > 0).map(([severity, count]) => `${count} ${severity}`)
428	  const who = review.verdict === 'blocked'
429	    ? `blocked by ${review.reviewers.filter(entry => entry.status === 'blocked').map(entry => entry.reviewer_id).join(', ') || 'review'}`
430	    : `approved by ${review.reviewers.map(entry => entry.reviewer_id).join(' and ')}`
431	  return [who, ...counts].join(' · ')
432	}
433	
434	function computeTimeline(run: RunData): Timeline {
435	  const { detail, inputs, review } = run
436	  const results = run.results ?? new Map<string, WorkerResult>()
437	  const rows = classify(detail, run.events)
438	  const spans: Span[] = []
439	  const open = new Map<string, Span>()
440	  const last = new Map<string, Span>()
441	  const openedBy = new Map<number, Span>()
442	  const closedBy = new Map<number, Span>()
443	  const reused = new Set<number>()
444	  const statusOf = (nodeId: string) => snapshotNode(detail, nodeId)?.status ?? 'pending'
445	  const at = (row: Row): Instant => ({ at: row.event.occurred_at, source: 'event' })
446	  const receiptWorkers = new Set((inputs?.workers ?? []).filter(worker => worker.launch).map(worker => worker.launch_node_id))
447	  const candidateRows: Row[] = []
448	
449	  // Rule 3: running opens a span for (node, attempt); the next terminal status closes it; a new attempt closes an open one as "no record".
450	  for (const row of rows) {
451	    const node = row.node
452	    if (!node || !row.status || row.marker || receiptWorkers.has(node)) continue
453	    if (node === 'candidate') { candidateRows.push(row); continue }
454	    const current = open.get(node)
455	    const previous = last.get(node)
456	    if (row.status === 'running' || row.status === 'awaiting_approval') {
457	      if (!current && previous && /^Resuming /.test(row.event.message)) {
458	        // A resumed freeze or review continues the same attempt.
459	        Object.assign(previous, { end: null, ms: null, status: row.status, outcome: row.text })
460	        open.set(node, previous)
461	        continue
462	      }
463	      const attempt = row.attempt ?? current?.attempt ?? (previous ? previous.attempt + 1 : Math.max(1, row.event.attempt))
464	      if (current && current.attempt !== attempt) {
465	        close(current, 'no_record', { ...at(row), note: 'ended without a record' }, 'ended without a record')
466	        closedBy.set(row.event.sequence, current)
467	        open.delete(node)
468	      }
469	      const span = open.get(node)
470	      if (span) { span.outcome = row.text; span.status = row.status; continue }
471	      const created = newSpan(node, laneOf(node), attempt, at(row))
472	      created.status = row.status
473	      created.outcome = row.text
474	      spans.push(created)
475	      open.set(node, created)
476	      last.set(node, created)
477	      openedBy.set(row.event.sequence, created)
478	    } else if (TERMINAL.has(row.status)) {
479	      if (current) {

1	import { describe, it } from 'node:test'
2	import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
3	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
4	import {
5	  validateReviewResult,
6	  validateRunDetail,
7	  validateRunInputs,
8	  type ReviewResult,
9	  type RunDetail,
10	  type RunInputs,
11	} from '../../contracts/projects/v1.ts'
12	import { eventSchema, validateWorkerResult, type WorkerResult, type WorkflowEvent } from '../../contracts/workflow/v1.ts'
13	import {
14	  attemptResultUris,
15	  buildTimeline,
16	  controllerNotRunning,
17	  deriveAttention,
18	  deriveFocus,
19	  deriveNow,
20	  gateReasonsByCheck,
21	  humanizeEvent,
22	  laneLines,
23	  nowResultUris,
24	  textToString,
25	  type Now,
26	  type RunData,
27	  type Span,
28	  type Step,
29	} from '../../contracts/projects/triage.ts'
30	
31	/**
32	 * The triage model (PRD_VIEWER_UX 5 and 6) on the captured skeleton-001 (blocked by review), skeleton-fixes-001
33	 * (succeeded) and workflow-guardrails-001 (two lanes, candidate failed identically) payloads, trimmed to what these
34	 * tests read and validated against the contracts, plus synthetic runs for situations no captured run reached. Results
35	 * the capture did not include (skeleton-001 game/1, guardrails controller/1 and candidate_ui/1) are derived below from
36	 * a captured sibling and the event that recorded their verdict, and are marked as such.
37	 */
38	
39	const ROOT = new URL('../../', import.meta.url)
40	
41	type Bundle = { detail: RunDetail; events: WorkflowEvent[]; inputs: RunInputs; review: ReviewResult | null; results: Map<string, WorkerResult> }
42	
43	function loadRun(name: string): Bundle {
44	  const raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL(`tests/unit/fixtures/runs/${name}.json`, ROOT), 'utf8')) as {
45	    detail: unknown; events: unknown[]; inputs: unknown; review: unknown; results: Record<string, unknown>
46	  }
47	  return {
48	    detail: validateRunDetail(raw.detail),
49	    events: raw.events.map(event => eventSchema.parse(event)),
50	    inputs: validateRunInputs(raw.inputs),
51	    review: raw.review === null ? null : validateReviewResult(raw.review),
52	    results: new Map(Object.entries(raw.results).map(([uri, result]) => [uri, validateWorkerResult(result)])),
53	  }
54	}
55	
56	const skeleton = loadRun('skeleton-001')
57	const fixes = loadRun('skeleton-fixes-001')
58	const guardrails = loadRun('workflow-guardrails-001')
59	
60	const SKELETON_RUN = '/api/projects/project-b/workflows/skeleton/runs/skeleton-001'
61	const GUARDRAILS_RUN = '/api/projects/md-manager/workflows/workflow-guardrails/runs/workflow-guardrails-001'
62	
63	const seconds = (from: string, to: string) => Math.round((Date.parse(to) - Date.parse(from)) / 1000)
64	const spanSeconds = (span: Span | undefined) => span?.ms === null || span?.ms === undefined ? null : Math.round(span.ms / 1000)
65	const eventAt = (bundle: Bundle, sequence: number) => bundle.events.find(event => event.sequence === sequence)!
66	
67	function shiftChecks(result: WorkerResult, lastFinish: string): WorkerResult['checks'] {
68	  const offset = Date.parse(lastFinish) - Date.parse(result.checks.at(-1)!.finished_at)
69	  const move = (iso: string) => new Date(Date.parse(iso) + offset).toISOString()
70	  return result.checks.map(check => ({ ...check, started_at: move(check.started_at), finished_at: move(check.finished_at) }))
71	}
72	
73	/** skeleton-001 results/game/1: served (HTTP 200) but not captured; its gate reasons are the ones event #14 recorded. */
74	const skeletonGame1 = validateWorkerResult({
75	  ...skeleton.results.get(`${SKELETON_RUN}/results/game/3`)!,
76	  attempt: 1, status: 'failed', error: { code: 'VERIFICATION_BLOCKED', message: eventAt(skeleton, 14).message, retryable: true },
77	})
78	/** guardrails results/controller/1: not captured; its gate reasons are the ones event #23 recorded. */
79	const guardrailsController1 = validateWorkerResult({
80	  ...guardrails.results.get(`${GUARDRAILS_RUN}/results/controller/2`)!,
81	  attempt: 1, status: 'failed', error: { code: 'VERIFICATION_BLOCKED', message: eventAt(guardrails, 23).message, retryable: true },
82	})
83	/** guardrails candidate_ui/1: not captured; it failed identically to /2 (RUNBOOK "Blocked after freeze"), its checks ending before event #28. */
84	const candidateUi2 = guardrails.results.get(`${GUARDRAILS_RUN}/results/candidate_ui/2`)!
85	const guardrailsCandidateUi1 = validateWorkerResult({ ...candidateUi2, attempt: 1, checks: shiftChecks(candidateUi2, '2026-09-23T20:24:50.300000Z') })
86	
87	function runData(bundle: Bundle, extra: Record<string, WorkerResult> = {}): RunData {
88	  return { detail: bundle.detail, events: bundle.events, inputs: bundle.inputs, review: bundle.review, results: new Map([...bundle.results, ...Object.entries(extra)]) }
89	}
90	
91	const guardrailsFull = () => runData(guardrails, { [`${GUARDRAILS_RUN}/results/candidate_ui/1`]: guardrailsCandidateUi1 })
92	
93	// ---- Synthetic single-lane runs on the skeleton-001 definition ------------------------------------------------------
94	
95	const T0 = Date.parse('2026-09-24T10:00:00Z')
96	const t = (second: number) => new Date(T0 + second * 1000).toISOString()
97	
98	type NodeState = NodeStatusName | [NodeStatusName, number]
99	type NodeStatusName = RunDetail['snapshot']['status']
100	type EventSpec = [second: number, node: string | null, status: NodeStatusName | null, message: string]
101	
102	function synthetic(options: {
103	  status: NodeStatusName
104	  nodes: Record<string, NodeState>
105	  events: EventSpec[]
106	  inputs?: (inputs: RunInputs) => void
107	  review?: ReviewResult | null
108	  results?: Record<string, WorkerResult>
109	}): RunData {
110	  const base = skeleton.detail
111	  const last = options.events.length ? Math.max(...options.events.map(([second]) => second)) : 0
112	  const summary = { ...base.summary, status: options.status, created_at: t(-60), updated_at: t(last + 1) }
113	  const nodes = base.snapshot.nodes.map(node => {
114	    const state = options.nodes[node.node_id] ?? 'pending'
115	    const [status, attempt] = Array.isArray(state) ? state : [state, state === 'pending' ? 0 : 1]
116	    return { ...node, status, attempt, session_id: null, result_uri: null, lane_results: [] }
117	  })
118	  const detail = validateRunDetail({ summary, definition: base.definition, snapshot: { ...base.snapshot, status: options.status, last_sequence: options.events.length, nodes } })
119	  const attempts = new Map<string, number>()
120	  const events = options.events.map(([second, node, status, message], index) => {
121	    const parsed = /\bAttempt (\d+)\b/.exec(message)
122	    if (node && parsed) attempts.set(node, Number(parsed[1]))
123	    return eventSchema.parse({
124	      contract_version: '1.0.0', run_id: 'skeleton-001', event_id: `skeleton-001:${index + 1}`, sequence: index + 1, occurred_at: t(second),
125	      node_id: node, attempt: node ? attempts.get(node) ?? 1 : 0, type: status ? 'status_changed' : 'log', status, message,
126	      artifact: null, result_uri: null, reused_from_attempt: null,
127	    })
128	  })
129	  const inputs = structuredClone(skeleton.inputs)
130	  const worker = inputs.workers[0]
131	  worker.launch = { ...worker.launch!, launch_requested_at: t(-2), native_started_at: t(0) }
132	  worker.stop = null
133	  worker.completion = null
134	  worker.handoff = null
135	  options.inputs?.(inputs)
136	  return { detail, events, inputs: validateRunInputs(inputs), review: options.review ?? null, results: new Map(Object.entries(options.results ?? {})) }
137	}
138	
139	const LAUNCHED: EventSpec[] = [
140	  [0, 'launch_game', 'running', 'Launching or reconciling the exact native session'],
141	  [3, 'launch_game', 'running', 'Awaiting explicit completion signal; idle is not acceptance'],
142	  [5, null, null, 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID 4242'],
143	]
144	const WORKING = { challenge: 'succeeded', launch_game: 'running' } as const
145	
146	// ---- Assertions shared by every deriveNow case ------------------------------------------------------------------
147	
148	const commands = (now: Now) => now.next.steps.filter((step): step is Extract<Step, { kind: 'command' }> => step.kind === 'command').map(step => step.text)
149	const prose = (now: Now) => [textToString(now.headline, T0), textToString(now.reason, T0), now.next.label, now.next.caveat ?? '',
150	  ...now.next.steps.map(step => step.kind === 'text' ? step.text : step.caption ?? '')].join('\n')
151	
152	const PYTHON = (file: string) => readFileSync(new URL(`workflow/${file}`, ROOT), 'utf8')
153	function body(source: string, header: string): string {
154	  const start = source.indexOf(header)
155	  assert.ok(start >= 0, `${header} exists`)
156	  const end = source.indexOf('\ndef ', start + header.length)
157	  return source.slice(start, end < 0 ? undefined : end)
158	}
159	const PIPELINE = body(PYTHON('pipeline.py'), 'def main(')
160	/** Where each verb's argparse lives (workflow/__main__.py dispatches launch, init, resume, answer and repair). */
161	const CLI: Record<string, string> = {
162	  launch: body(PYTHON('launch.py'), 'def main('),
163	  init: body(PYTHON('scaffold.py'), 'def main('),
164	  resume: body(PYTHON('guardrails.py'), 'def resume_main('),
165	  answer: body(PYTHON('guardrails.py'), 'def answer_main('),
166	  repair: body(PYTHON('repair.py'), 'def repair_main('),
167	  'attach-one': body(PYTHON('interactive.py'), 'def main('),
168	}
169	
170	/** Every command is the RUNBOOK form `"$PY" -m workflow[.interactive] <verb> ...`, and each verb and flag exists in that verb's argparse. */
171	function assertRealCli(now: Now) {
172	  for (const command of commands(now)) {
173	    const tokens = command.match(/"[^"]*"|\S+/g)!
174	    assert.equal(tokens[0], '"$PY"', command)
175	    assert.equal(tokens[1], '-m', command)
176	    const verb = tokens[3]
177	    const parser = CLI[verb] ?? PIPELINE
178	    assert.equal(tokens[2], verb === 'attach-one' ? 'workflow.interactive' : 'workflow', command)
179	    assert.ok(parser.includes(verb === 'attach-one' ? '"attach-one"' : CLI[verb] ? 'argparse' : `"${verb}"`), `${verb} is a CLI action (${command})`)
180	    for (const flag of tokens.filter(token => token.startsWith('--'))) assert.ok(parser.includes(`add_argument("${flag}"`), `${verb} takes ${flag} (${command})`)
181	    if (tokens.includes('"$RUN"')) assert.equal(tokens[4], '"$RUN"', `the run directory follows the verb (${command})`)
182	  }
183	}
184	
185	const RUNBOOK = readFileSync(new URL('workflow/RUNBOOK.md', ROOT), 'utf8').split('\n')
186	function assertRunbook(now: Now) {
187	  assert.ok(now.next.runbook.length > 0 || ['running', 'inactive'].includes(now.situation), 'names its RUNBOOK section')
188	  for (const ref of now.next.runbook) {
189	    const start = RUNBOOK.findIndex(line => /^#{1,4} /.test(line) && line.replace(/^#+ /, '') === ref.section)
190	    assert.ok(start >= 0, `RUNBOOK has the section "${ref.section}"`)
191	    const level = RUNBOOK[start].indexOf(' ')
192	    const next = RUNBOOK.findIndex((line, index) => index > start && /^#{1,4} /.test(line) && line.indexOf(' ') <= level)
193	    if (ref.topic) assert.ok(RUNBOOK.slice(start, next < 0 ? undefined : next).join('\n').includes(`**${ref.topic}`), `"${ref.section}" has the topic "${ref.topic}"`)
194	  }
195	}
196	
197	function checked(run: Parameters<typeof deriveNow>[0]): Now {
198	  const now = deriveNow(run)
199	  assertRealCli(now)
200	  assertRunbook(now)
201	  assert.ok(commands(now).every(command => !/git push|\bmerge\b/.test(command)), 'never a push or merge command')
202	  return now
203	}
204	
205	// ---- buildTimeline -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
206	
207	describe('buildTimeline', () => {
208	  const timeline = buildTimeline(runData(skeleton))
209	
210	  it('re-reads challenge attempts 1-3 from the messages; attempt 1 ended without a record', () => {
211	    const challenge = timeline.byNode.get('challenge') ?? []
212	    assert.deepEqual(challenge.map(span => [span.attempt, span.status]), [[1, 'no_record'], [2, 'failed'], [3, 'succeeded']])
213	    assert.deepEqual(challenge.map(spanSeconds), [seconds(eventAt(skeleton, 1).occurred_at, eventAt(skeleton, 2).occurred_at), 47, 149])
214	    assert.equal(spanSeconds(challenge[0]), 373)
215	    assert.match(challenge[1].outcome, /interrupted \(KeyboardInterrupt\)/)

217	
218	  it('spans the worker from its launch and stop receipts: 28m21s', () => {
219	    const [worker] = timeline.byNode.get('launch_game') ?? []
220	    assert.equal(worker.start?.source, 'receipt')
221	    assert.equal(worker.end?.source, 'receipt')
222	    assert.equal(worker.start?.at, '2026-09-24T08:50:52.345Z')
223	    assert.equal(spanSeconds(worker), 28 * 60 + 21)

226	
227	  it('times the verify attempts 1m07s, 1m07s and 1m15s, attempt 3 split into setup 42s and checks 33s', () => {
228	    const verify = timeline.byNode.get('verify_game') ?? []
229	    assert.deepEqual(verify.map(span => [span.attempt, span.status, spanSeconds(span)]), [[1, 'failed', 67], [2, 'failed', 67], [3, 'succeeded', 75]])
230	    assert.equal(verify[2].result_uri, `${SKELETON_RUN}/results/game/3`)
231	    assert.deepEqual(verify[2].split && [Math.round(verify[2].split.setup_ms / 1000), Math.round(verify[2].split.checks_ms / 1000)], [42, 33])
232	  })
233	
234	  it('turns the node-less diagnosis and repair rows into markers, with the 5m37s of operator time between them', () => {
235	    const diagnosis = timeline.markers.find(marker => marker.kind === 'diagnosis')
236	    assert.equal(diagnosis?.lane, 'game')
237	    assert.equal(diagnosis?.node_id, 'verify_game')
238	    assert.equal(diagnosis?.at, eventAt(skeleton, 19).occurred_at)
239	    const repair = timeline.markers.find(marker => marker.kind === 'repair')
240	    assert.deepEqual(repair?.repair, { n: 1, snapshot: '50b14b3c', files: ['tests/reporters/testSummary.ts', 'tests/unit/testSummary.test.ts', 'vitest.config.ts'] })
241	    assert.equal(repair?.node_id, 'verify_game')
242	    const operator = timeline.gaps.filter(gap => gap.kind === 'operator')
243	    assert.deepEqual(operator.map(gap => [gap.from, Math.round(gap.ms / 1000)]), [[diagnosis?.at, 5 * 60 + 37]])
244	    assert.ok(timeline.activity.some(row => row.kind === 'gap' && row.gap?.kind === 'operator'), 'the gap is an Activity row')
245	    assert.ok(timeline.markers.every(marker => marker.kind !== 'controller_blocked'), 'the diagnosis is not also a second blocked marker')

248	  it('infers the print-transport review start from the candidate: ≈2m10s', () => {
249	    const [review] = timeline.byNode.get('review') ?? []
250	    assert.equal(review.start?.source, 'inferred')
251	    assert.equal(review.start?.at, eventAt(skeleton, 25).occurred_at)
252	    assert.equal(review.end?.source, 'review')
253	    assert.equal(spanSeconds(review), 130)
254	    assert.equal(review.status, 'failed')
255	    const [candidate] = timeline.byNode.get('candidate') ?? []
256	    assert.equal(candidate.start?.source, 'inferred')

262	  it('spans the run from creation to the last non-controller activity: 52m51s ending 09:32:31, not updated_at', () => {
263	    assert.equal(timeline.runEnd?.at, skeleton.review!.reviewed_at)

270	  it('lists Activity oldest first: an attempt that ended without a record gets its own row, the verdicts read as outcomes', () => {
271	    const challenge = timeline.activity.filter(row => row.node_id === 'challenge').slice(0, 3)
272	    assert.deepEqual(challenge.map(row => [row.kind, row.text]), [
273	      ['start', 'attempt 1 started (print job, session f18dee3c-424c-4e3e-9379-a7ad784c9e37)'],
274	      ['end', 'attempt 1 ended without a record'],
275	      ['start', 'attempt 2 started after re-pinning the feature files (base 313eb87)'],

279	    assert.deepEqual([review?.kind, review?.source, review?.text, review?.inferred], ['end', 'review', 'blocked by general · 1 P1 · 3 P2', true])
280	    const tail = buildTimeline(runData(fixes)).activity.slice(-3).map(row => [row.node_id, row.text])
281	    assert.deepEqual(tail, [
282	      ['review', 'approved by general and coverage · 3 P2'],
283	      ['approval', 'approved · no approval event recorded'],
284	      ['integrate', 'fast-forwarded to ee74298 · no push performed'],

290	    const pid = timeline.activity.filter(row => row.controller_log)

295	  describe('guardrails (two lanes, a lane named controller)', () => {
296	    const run = buildTimeline(guardrailsFull())
297	
298	    it('turns PID and [Errno] rows aliased onto launch_controller into controller markers, never a node running or failed', () => {
299	      assert.equal(run.markers.filter(marker => marker.kind === 'controller_start').length, 8)

355	// ---- deriveNow: one case per data-situation ------------------------------------------------------------------------
356	
357	describe('deriveNow', () => {
358	  it('review_blocked', () => {
359	    const now = checked(runData(skeleton))
360	    assert.equal(now.situation, 'review_blocked')

364	    const reason = textToString(now.reason, T0)
365	    assert.match(reason, /general blocked the candidate: 1 open P1 — Private matches can be joined without their code\./)
366	    assert.match(reason, /coverage was superseded \(no verdict\)/)
367	    assert.deepEqual(now.next.steps.map(step => step.kind), ['command', 'text', 'command'])

369	      '"$PY" -m workflow init <fixes-feature> --repo <target repo>',

373	    const everything = JSON.stringify(now.next)
374	    for (const invented of ['skeleton', 'Pirate', 'skeleton-001', '<run id>']) assert.ok(!everything.includes(invented), `no concrete ${invented}`)

377	  it('blocked_identical', () => {
378	    const now = checked(guardrailsFull())

1	# Handoff: Viewer UX slice S2, the triage model
2	
3	Slice S2 of [PRD_VIEWER_UX.md](../PRD_VIEWER_UX.md) (section 11). Branch `ux/s2`, made from `feature/viewer-ux`. S2 changes nothing in `src/`, `server/`, `package.json` or any browser spec.
4	
5	## What shipped
6	
7	`contracts/projects/triage.ts` is new. It is pure TypeScript: it imports only types and `isBlockingFinding` from `v1.ts`, and it uses no React, no DOM and no I/O. The client (S3) and the server (S5) can both import it. Its exports:
8	
9	| Export | PRD | What it gives |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| `buildTimeline(run)` | 5.1, 5.2 rules 1-11 | `runStart`, `runEnd`, `lastActivity`, `spans` (one per node attempt, per lane for the candidate), `markers`, `gaps`, `byNode` and `activity` (the Activity rows, oldest first, with PID rows flagged `controller_log`). It is memoized per run on the served state. |
12	| `deriveNow(run)` | 6.2 | `situation` (the `data-situation` id), `interruption` (rule 5 case a-d), `tone`, `glyph`, `focus`, `lane`, `since`, `headline`, `reason` and `reasonSource` (0-4), `next` and `missing` |
13	| `deriveFocus(detail, events)` | 6.2 focus rule | the focus node with its label, kind, status and `since` |
14	| `deriveAttention(run)` | 6.4 | `top` (question > pane > approval) and `nodes`, one kind per node, for `data-attention` |
15	| `humanizeEvent(event)` | 5.3 | known phrases reworded, SHAs cut to 7 characters, session UUIDs kept whole, the B1 `[lane] ` prefix dropped |
16	| `gateReasonsByCheck(message, checks)` | 4.6 | `reasons`, `gate` (unkeyed) and `byCheck`. A `<path>` tail is attached to a check only when exactly one check's command ends with it. |
17	| `attemptResultUris(detail, node, {last})` | 4.4 | the `results/<lane>/<k>` and `results/candidate_<lane>/<k>` URIs, oldest first per lane |
18	| `nowResultUris(detail)` | 6.2 source 2 | what the Now banner and the lanes line read: the failing focus's latest two attempts, plus each lane's candidate result when there are 2 or more lanes |
19	| `laneLines(run)` | 4.2 lanes line | one line per lane (worker · verify · candidate) for runs with 2 or more lanes, else `[]` |
20	| `controllerNotRunning(readings)` | 6.3 | the 15 s `not_running` debounce, used by rule 5(c) and the S6 chip |
21	| `textToString(text, now, format)`, `plainTextFormat` | — | flattens the rich `Text` parts. S3 passes S1's zone-aware formatters, or renders the parts itself. |
22	| `COMMAND_CAPTION`, `COMMAND_LEGEND`, `MAX_QUESTIONS`, `CONTROLLER_DEBOUNCE_MS`, `GAP_MS` | 6.1, 6.3 | fixed wording and limits |
23	
24	**Next steps are data.** `next` has this shape:
25	
26	```
27	{ action: 'required' | 'none' | 'unknown', label, runbook: {section, topic}[], steps: ({kind:'command', text, caption?} | {kind:'text', text})[], caveat }
28	```
29	
30	- Commands use the RUNBOOK form, `"$PY" -m workflow <verb> "$RUN" …`.
31	- Every value the viewer cannot know stays a placeholder: `<fixes-feature>`, `<target repo>`, `<new run id>`, `<sha>`, `"<why>"`, `"<reason>"` and `"<your answer>"`. The one filled-in value is the approval hash, which comes from the review.
32	
33	**Rich text.** The headline and the reason are arrays of plain strings mixed with these parts:
34	
35	- `{kind:'clock', at}`: a time of day
36	- `{kind:'ago', at}`: a relative time
37	- `{kind:'span', ms}`: a duration
38	- `{kind:'elapsed', from}`: time since an instant
39	- `{kind:'left', until}`: time until an instant
40	
41	The model therefore holds no time zone and no `now`. The UI renders the parts as `<time>` elements with S1's formatters and its ticking `useNow`.
42	
43	**Fixtures.** Three trimmed fixtures are in `tests/unit/fixtures/runs/`: `skeleton-001.json`, `skeleton-fixes-001.json` and `workflow-guardrails-001.json`.
44	- Each holds `{detail, events, inputs, review, results}`, taken from the captured `ux/api/*.json` payloads.
45	- Only text the tests never read was shortened: task and prompt texts, `decisions.md`, long summaries and file artifacts.
46	- The test validates every fixture against the contracts when it loads it.
47	- The capture has no `results/game/1` for skeleton-001, and no `results/controller/1` or `results/candidate_ui/1` for guardrails. The test derives each of them from a captured sibling result plus the event that recorded its verdict. The test file's header documents this.
48	
49	## Red evidence
50	
51	The tests were written first against a skeleton `triage.ts`. Its types were final and its functions returned empty values, or `no_rule_matched` with no RUNBOOK section. It was run with:
52	
53	```
54	npx tsx --test tests/unit/triage.test.ts
55	ℹ tests 46   ℹ pass 1   ℹ fail 45        (42 AssertionError, 3 TypeError from destructuring empty span lists)
56	```
57	
58	Key failing lines:
59	
60	```
61	re-reads challenge attempts 1-3 …        actual: []  expected: [[1,'no_record'],[2,'failed'],[3,'succeeded']]
62	times the verify attempts …              actual: []  expected: [[1,'failed',67],[2,'failed',67],[3,'succeeded',75]]
63	diagnosis and repair markers …           actual: undefined  expected: 'game'
64	spans the run … 52m51s                   actual: undefined  expected: '2026-09-24T09:32:31.411386Z'
65	keeps PID checkpoints in the controller log   actual: 0  expected: 5
66	is memoized …                            Values have same structure but are not reference-equal
67	deriveNow review_blocked … (all 20 cases)     AssertionError: names its RUNBOOK section   (the stub answers no_rule_matched with no section)
68	gateReasonsByCheck (3 cases)             actual: []  expected: ['unit','integration'] / ['project-workflows-browser'] / gate-level + attached
69	deriveAttention orders question > pane > approval   actual: undefined  expected: 'question'
70	humanizeEvent                            actual: 'Awaiting explicit completion signal; idle is not acceptance'  expected: "waiting for the worker's completion signal …"
71	laneLines                                actual: []  expected: two lane lines
72	```
73	
74	Only one test passed against the skeleton, and it passed vacuously: "clears a pane once any later event names that node" asserts that there is no attention, which is exactly what the stub returns.
75	
76	The first red run was made before the Activity-ordering test existed. That test was added after green, to pin the polish described below. The whole final test file was then run again against the saved skeleton, which gave the counts above, and the implementation was restored (its sha256 was checked).
77	
78	**Test-authoring mistakes, fixed before the first red run and not product reds:**
79	1. The synthetic runs inherited skeleton-001's launch receipt at 08:50, so the expected deadline in the `running` case was wrong. `synthetic()` now puts `native_started_at` at the run's t0.
80	2. The scope case built an event tuple with a `null as never` placeholder. It was rewritten as a plain sorted list.
81	3. The approval case expected "(12 min)" and the running case expected "5m ago", which assumed a coarser duration format than the model's parts render. They now expect the relative part ("12 min ago") and the span part ("5m00s").
82	
83	**Product bugs found on the way to green:**
84	1. The first full run failed 4 tests with `TypeError … reading 'status'`: the candidate-result lookup built nested arrays. It is fixed with a flat map.
85	2. `tsc` then reported an unused parameter, which was removed.
86	3. A read-through of the model's output on the three real runs found four rough edges, all fixed and now pinned by the Activity test:
87	   - An event that ended one attempt and opened the next showed as a single "end" row.
88	   - The review's closing row showed raw session ids instead of the verdict.
89	   - The inferred approval row sorted after the integrate row that shares its instant.
90	   - The repair note carried a "(restated)" suffix.
91	
92	## Green evidence
93	
94	```
95	npx tsx --test tests/unit/triage.test.ts              ℹ tests 46  ℹ pass 46  ℹ fail 0
96	npx tsc -b                                            exit 0
97	npx eslint contracts/projects/triage.ts tests/unit/triage.test.ts   exit 0
98	```
99	
100	The unit tests cover every case in 12.1:
101	- the `buildTimeline` items;
102	- one `deriveNow` case per `data-situation`: `review_blocked`, `blocked_identical`, `succeeded`, `question` (export and event log), `pane_attention` (worker, reviewer, and cleared by a later event), `interrupted` cases a, b-review, b-freeze, c and d (automatic and retry), `blocked_before_freeze` ×4, `challenge_paused`, `awaiting_approval`, `check_failed` (automatic and manual), `running`, `inactive`, `no_rule_matched` (failed and paused), and scope;
103	- `gateReasonsByCheck` ×3, `deriveAttention` ×2, focus, humanize, URIs and lanes.
104	
105	Every `deriveNow` case also passes two checks against the real sources:
106	- **CLI.** Each command's verb and every `--flag` must appear in the argparse of the module that owns the verb: `pipeline.py` `main`, `guardrails.py` `resume_main` and `answer_main`, `repair.py` `repair_main`, `scaffold.py` `main`, `launch.py` `main` and `interactive.py` `main`. `"$RUN"` must directly follow the verb.
107	- **RUNBOOK.** Each `runbook` reference must be an exact `workflow/RUNBOOK.md` heading, and its topic must be a `**bold**` label inside that section.
108	
109	No Playwright was run. S2 has no browser scenario in 12.2 and no migration in 12.3, and it changes no component, spec or `src/` file.
110	
111	## Migrations
112	
113	None. S2 changes no existing file.
114	
115	## Deviations from the PRD
116	
117	**API shape**
118	
119	1. **`buildTimeline` input.** It takes `{detail, events, inputs?, review?, results?}` instead of `{definition, snapshot, events, inputs, review?, laneResults?, now}`. It takes no `now`: a live span has `end: null` and `live: true`, and the UI measures it with its own clock, so the memoized timeline does not go stale every second.
120	   - `results` is a map from result URI to result. Lane matching and the setup/check split read it.
121	2. **Memo key.** It is a superset of the PRD's key: `last_sequence`, the run and node statuses, attempts and result URIs, the event count and last sequence, and the inputs, review and results objects by identity.
122	3. **`controller_blocked` marker kind.** It is added to the union: 5.2 rule 5 names it, but 5.1's list omits it. A "failed identically" row is one `diagnosis` marker with `blocked: true`, not two markers.
123	4. **Activity rows.** `Timeline.activity` is an addition beyond 5.1's return shape, so S3 can render Activity directly. `lastActivity` includes the review verdict and the stop receipts; B2's `last_activity_at` is defined over raw events only.
124	5. **Rich text.** Headlines are rich text. The approval's "(12 min)" renders from an `ago` part as "12 min ago", and "working 5m" renders through the span formatter.
125	
126	**Classification of controller rows**
127	
128	6. **Stop-confirmation failures.** A `Could not confirm worker stop: …` failure that the controller recovered from is a `controller_error` marker, not a handoff failure. Recovered means a later PID checkpoint, or the node succeeded later. Guardrails #7, #10, #13 and #16 are examples. PRD rule 2 names only `^[Errno` failures.
129	7. **B1's rule, applied in the client until B1 lands.** Rows on `launch_controller` that match B1's controller-process patterns are treated as run-level. 5.2 rule 2 intends this.
130	
131	**Timeline values**
132	
133	8. **Gap rows.** No gap row is emitted while a non-worker step is running, because that step's bar already shows the time. The PRD's catch-all is "no activity".
134	   - The PRD's "worker working 28m21s" is the worker's span. The gap itself runs from the last PID row to the stop receipt: 28m18s.
135	9. **Rounding.** Durations round to the nearest second, which matches the PRD's 1m07s, 1m06s, 2m10s and 52m51s. Two PRD values differ:
136	   - Challenge attempt 2 is 46.8 s, so it shows as 47s; the wireframe says 46s.
137	   - Guardrails' run span is 54m20s under rule 10. PRD 4.1 says 54m21s, which counts the trailing PID row that rule 10 excludes.
138	10. **Focus ties.** "Ties go to the latest event" is read as nodes in the same graph column, meaning parallel lanes. Among those, the latest status event wins, then definition order.
139	
140	**Situation rules**
141	
142	11. **Rule 1 (question).** A question counts only while the run is not finished and the lane has not been stopped, because `answer` refuses once the worker went on.
143	12. **Rule 3 (awaiting approval).** Two command forms go beyond the PRD:
144	    - A manual review gate that awaits the import gets `review "$RUN" --review-file <review.json>`, with a text step about `--reviewer <id>` (RUNBOOK §5).
145	    - A manual handoff gets one `freeze "$RUN"` command with a `--handoff <lane>=<lane-handoff.json>` flag per lane, which is the RUNBOOK §4 form.
146	13. **Rule 5 (d), repair continuation.** The rule also matches a paused candidate after a candidate repair. It takes the `Continue with …` text from the latest `Repair n by the operator` note on a `verify_<lane>` node, because repair.py:442 writes the note there. The candidate's own note is "Repair n supersedes …".
147	14. **Rule 7 (blocked, identical failure).** Step 4, "the same without --dry-run", is a copyable command with a caption rather than plain text.
148	15. **Rule 8 (check failed) on an automatic run.** The rule needs the run to be `running`. A failed automatic run with attempts left was stopped by something else, so it falls to rule 13.
149	16. **Reviewer panes.** The target is `--node review` for the built-in reviewer and `--node review-<id>` for a declared one (interactive.py `--node` help).
150	
151	**Scope**
152	
153	17. **Extra exports.** `nowResultUris`, `controllerNotRunning`, `textToString`, `plainTextFormat` and the constants go beyond the PRD's list. Consumers need them, and they keep the rules in one place.
154	18. **Size.** `triage.ts` is about 1,430 lines against the PRD's estimate of about 400. Most of the difference is the 13 situation builders with their command tables, the Activity rows and the doc comments. The test file is about 760 lines.
155	
156	## Follow-ups
157	
158	- **S3.**
159	  - Fetch `nowResultUris(detail)` before trusting the banner, and treat a non-empty `Now.missing` as "loading". Without `candidate_ui/1`, guardrails reads `no_rule_matched` and lists that URI in `missing`.
160	  - Render `Text` parts with S1's `Time`, `formatSpan` and `formatAgo`, or pass a `TextFormat`.
161	  - Hide `controller_log` rows behind "Controller log (n)".
162	- **S5.** Use `deriveFocus` and `humanizeEvent` for B2's `focus` and `headline`. The client already reads:
163	  - B1's statuses on node-less rows (`failed` means controller_blocked; `paused` means interrupted);
164	  - the `[<lane>] ` candidate prefix, both for lane matching and in `humanizeEvent`.
165	
166	  Once B1 serves correct attempts, the client's re-parse of `attempt N` still agrees with them.
167	- **S6.**
168	  - `controllerNotRunning` gives the chip's 15 s debounce.
169	  - `deriveNow` and `deriveAttention` take a `ServedActivity` (`waiting_questions`, `attention`) as a fallback. It follows B2's field names, so S5's `v1.ts` type should stay assignable to it.
170	- **Known limit (C6).** Before B1, the lane-specific blocked rows of a lane named `controller` are aliased onto `launch_controller` as node failures. An example is "Worker controller deadline exhausted". Rule 6 cannot quote such a row, so the run falls to rule 13, which still shows the message as reason source 4.
171	- **`test:unit` glob.** S1 adds `tests/unit/*.test.ts` to it. Until then, run `npx tsx --test tests/unit/triage.test.ts`.

        if number > MAX_QUESTIONS:

        at = (clock or time.time)()

        entry = {"n": number, "question": item["question"], "asked_at": iso(at), "answer": None, "answered_at": None}

        deadline = load_deadline(directory, node)

def completion_signal(directory: Path, plan: dict, node: str, questions: list) -> dict | None:
    """The worker's completion file as the controller reads it (`automatic.read_signal`); null when the controller refuses it.

    A missing, malformed, stale or foreign file, or one of another version than the run pinned, is not the worker's signal.
    `version` is that pinned version: a 1.0.0 completion has no evidence (null), and an empty 1.1.0 field is null too. A
    `question` after the lane's third recorded question is served as `blocked`, as `record_question` treats it; `question`
    carries the text of a question the controller has not recorded, and is null for every other completion.
    """
    from .automatic import read_signal
    try:
        item = read_signal(SimpleNamespace(directory=directory, plan=plan), node)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    status = "blocked" if item["status"] == "question" and len(questions) >= MAX_QUESTIONS else item["status"]
    untested = item.get("untested")
    return {"version": item["version"], "status": status, "summary": item["summary"], "open_assumptions": list(item["open_assumptions"]),
            "untested": list(untested) if isinstance(untested, list) else None,
            "falsifying_check": optional_text(item.get("falsifying_check")), "verify_yourself": optional_text(item.get("verify_yourself")),
            "question": item["question"] if item["status"] == "question" else None}


QUESTION_KEYS = ("n", "question", "asked_at", "answer", "answered_at")


def worker_questions(path: Path) -> list:
    """`<node>.questions.json` as `{n, question, asked_at, answer, answered_at}` entries; `[]` when absent or malformed."""
    item = load_optional(path)
    questions = item.get("questions") if isinstance(item, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(questions, list):
        return []
    result = []
    for entry in questions:
        if (not isinstance(entry, dict) or type(entry.get("n")) is not int or not optional_text(entry.get("question"))
                or not isinstance(entry.get("asked_at"), str) or not (entry.get("answer") is None or isinstance(entry.get("answer"), str))
                or not (entry.get("answered_at") is None or isinstance(entry.get("answered_at"), str))
                or (entry.get("answer") is None) != (entry.get("answered_at") is None)):
            return []
        result.append({key: entry.get(key) for key in QUESTION_KEYS})
    return result

    Controller: export run-state.json after every graph step
    
    One graph.invoke runs freeze, checks, candidate and review, and the export was

content.content:
def went_on(directory: Path, node: str) -> str | None:
    """What shows the worker went on from its latest question, or None: record_question moved that question's file away,
    so a completion file is its next signal; a saved handoff or a stop follows one. A stopped worker's pane is a shell."""
    for name, reason in (("stop", "stopped by the controller"), ("handoff", "its handoff saved"), ("completion", "its next completion signal written")):
        if (directory / f"{node}.{name}.json").exists():
            return reason
    return None


def record_answer(directory: Path, node: str, text: str, clock=None, delivered: bool | None = None) -> dict:
    """The latest question's answer; the deadline restarts now. Refused when no question waits.

    `answer` records `delivered: false` and sets it once the text reached the worker, so a failed delivery can be
    retried. It also replaces PANE_ANSWER, which the controller records (without the flag) once the session works
    again: that deadline already runs, and the text still reaches the worker while it is on that question. Once it
    went on, the text would reach no question (or a shell), so nothing is recorded.
    """
    if not text.strip():
        raise ValueError("The answer is empty")
    with question_lock(directory):
        questions = load_questions(directory, node)
        if not questions or questions[-1]["answer"] not in {None, PANE_ANSWER}:
            raise ValueError(f"Worker {node} has no unanswered question")
        reason = went_on(directory, node)
        if reason:
            raise ValueError(f"Worker {node} has no unanswered question: it went on from question {questions[-1]['n']} ({reason}); "
                             "nothing is typed into its pane")
        at = (clock or time.time)()
        questions[-1].update(answer=text, answered_at=iso(at))
        if delivered is not None:
            questions[-1]["delivered"] = delivered
        save_questions(directory, node, questions)
        resume_deadline(directory, node, at)
    return questions[-1]


def record_pane_answer(directory: Path, node: str, clock=None) -> dict | None:
    """The session works again while its latest question waits: PANE_ANSWER, and the deadline runs again.

    Checked and written under the lock: when `answer` recorded the answer meanwhile, nothing is recorded (None).
    """
    with question_lock(directory):
        questions = load_questions(directory, node)
        if not questions or questions[-1]["answer"] is not None:
            return None
        at = (clock or time.time)()
        questions[-1].update(answer=PANE_ANSWER, answered_at=iso(at))
        save_questions(directory, node, questions)
        resume_deadline(directory, node, at)
    return questions[-1]


def undelivered_answer(directory: Path, node: str, text: str) -> dict | None:
    """The latest question when `answer` recorded this text but never delivered it: a rerun delivers it, recording nothing.

    A different text is refused: a question is answered once, and its deadline already runs again. So is any rerun once
    the worker went on: the text would reach no question (or a shell).
    """
    questions = load_questions(directory, node)
    if not questions or questions[-1]["answer"] is None or questions[-1].get("delivered") is not False:
        return None
def answer_main(argv=None):
    """The deadline restarts when the answer is recorded (PRD 4.6), before the delivery, and stays running when the delivery
    fails: paused until a delivery, it would never run again if the operator then typed the answer in the pane (the
    controller records a pane answer only while the question waits). A rerun delivers the recorded answer within it."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m workflow answer", description="Answer a worker's question: record it, restart the "
                                     "worker's deadline and type it into the worker's pane. Rerun it to deliver an answer whose delivery failed.")
    parser.add_argument("directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("node", help="The lane whose latest question this answers")
    parser.add_argument("text")
    parser.add_argument("--no-herdr", action="store_true", help="Print the claude attach command instead of typing into the pane")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    directory = args.directory.resolve()
    entry = delivered = None
    try:
        plan = read_json(directory / "plan.json")
        if args.node not in plan_workers(plan):
            raise ValueError(f"{args.node} is not a lane of this run ({', '.join(plan_workers(plan))})")
        entry = undelivered_answer(directory, args.node, args.text)
        if entry is None:
            entry = record_answer(directory, args.node, args.text, delivered=False)
            print(f"Recorded the answer to question {entry['n']} of {args.node}; its deadline runs again.")
        else:
            typed = " (typed into its pane, not submitted)" if entry.get("typed") else ""
            print(f"Question {entry['n']} of {args.node} was answered at {entry['answered_at']} and never delivered{typed}; delivering it now "
                  "(nothing is recorded again, and its deadline has run since).")
        print(deliver_answer(directory, args.node, entry, not args.no_herdr))
        delivered = True
        mark_delivered(directory, args.node, entry["n"])
    except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        if delivered:
            parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\nThe answer reached the worker but is not marked delivered; do not rerun answer for this question.\n")
        if entry is not None and entry.get("typed"):
            parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\nThe answer to question {entry['n']} was typed into the worker's pane but not submitted; its "
                           f"deadline runs. Rerunning from a Herdr pane presses Enter only, never types the text again, and only while the pane "
                           f"shows the answer in the session's input (a session an update respawned starts with an empty one):\n"
                           f"  {answer_command(directory, args.node, args.text)}\nor look at the pane and print the claude attach command to submit "
                           f"it yourself (press Enter if the session's input holds the answer, else type it first):\n"
                           f"  {answer_command(directory, args.node, args.text, herdr=False)}\n")
        if entry is not None:
            parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\nThe answer to question {entry['n']} stays recorded and its deadline runs, but it did not reach "
                           f"the worker. Deliver it by rerunning, from a Herdr pane:\n  {answer_command(directory, args.node, args.text)}\n"
                           f"or print the claude attach command and type it yourself:\n  {answer_command(directory, args.node, args.text, herdr=False)}\n")
        parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\n")
